newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai parliament dissolved, election Nov 17.
newsitem.headline: Thai parliament dissolved, election Nov 17.

text.p: Thailand's King Bhumbibol Adulyadej issued a royal proclamation on Friday dissolving parliament and setting November 17 as the date for fresh elections, state-owned Radio Thailand said.
The proclamation was made more than an hour after a deputy premier and close ally of the outgoing Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa told reporters a dissolution was to be announced.
Banharn went on television soon after the royal proclamation to explain the reasons for his surprise decision to dissolve parliament and call a snap election.
He had been widely expected to quit after promising to resign within seven days last Saturday under pressure from key allies in his six-party coaition government.

Many politicians and analysts had expected his Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh to succeed him, but Banharn's supporters in his main Chart Thai party refused to support Chavalit who they sawas as the architect of the premier's downfall.
